record.original_question: Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of k-orbit polytopes.

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of k-orbit polytopes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope is a graded partially ordered set P with a unique minimum and unique maximum element, whose maximal chains (called flags) all have the same length n+1, which is strongly flag-connected, and which satisfies the diamond condition (for any chain missing exactly one element of an intermediate rank, there are exactly two ways to extend it to a flag). The automorphism group Γ(P) acts on the set of flags, and P is called a k-orbit polytope if this action has exactly k orbits; when k=1, P is regular.

A (geometric) realization of an abstract n-polytope P is, roughly, a mapping β from the vertex set of P into a Euclidean space (extended in a compatible way to higher-rank faces by taking convex hulls/affine images) which is compatible with the symmetry structure of P; for regular (1-orbit) polytopes, a well-developed theory of realizations exists in which the moduli space of realizations forms a convex cone, and the symmetric (regular) realizations correspond to the orthogonal representations of the automorphism group, with irreducible realizations corresponding to irreducible representations.

A "matched" or "k-orbit" realization of a k-orbit polytope should be a realization in which the symmetry of the realization (as a configuration in Euclidean space) reflects the k-orbit structure of P, i.e. the realization has exactly k flag orbits under its geometric symmetry group, matching the abstract orbit structure.

Problem. Develop a theory of k-orbit realizations of k-orbit abstract polytopes that extends the classical realization theory of regular abstract polytopes. In particular, define the moduli space of k-orbit (matched) realizations of a given k-orbit abstract polytope P, identify its structure (e.g. as a convex cone), describe a notion of irreducible k-orbit realizations and a decomposition of arbitrary k-orbit realizations into irreducibles, and connect these objects to the representation theory of the automorphism group Γ(P) and of the flag-stabilizer subgroups corresponding to the k flag orbits.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a list of open problems on k-orbit abstract polytopes published in Discrete Mathematics. While realization theory for regular (1-orbit) polytopes is well-developed (notably by McMullen and Schulte) and there has been related work on rooted polytopes and on characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit polytopes (e.g. Hubard et al., 2022), no comprehensive theory of k-orbit (matched) realizations for general k-orbit polytopes has been established. The problem appears to remain open.
